```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

```{r}
library(z3r)
ctx <- z3_context()
x <- z3_int(ctx, "x")
y <- z3_int(ctx, "y")
```

## The three answers

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x > 0, x < 3)
z3_check(s)

s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x > 0, x < 1)
z3_check(s)
```

The third answer, `"unknown"`, means Z3 stopped without deciding. It is
never a disguised `"unsat"`:

```{r}
z <- z3_int(ctx, "z")
s <- z3_solver(ctx, timeout = 300)
z3_add(s, x > 0, y > 0, z > 0, x^3 + y^3 == z^3)
z3_check(s)
z3_reason_unknown(s)
```

Use `timeout` (milliseconds) or the deterministic `rlimit` to bound a check;
Ctrl-C also interrupts one. `z3_param_help(s)` lists every solver parameter
and `z3_set_params()` sets them with type checking:

```{r, error = TRUE}
z3_set_params(s, random_seed = 7, timeout = 1000)
z3_set_params(s, timeout = "soon")
```

## Models

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x + y == 10, x > 2 * y, y > 0)
z3_check(s)
m <- z3_model(s)
m
z3_eval(m, x * y)
z3_model_values(m)
```

`z3_eval()` leaves constants the model does not mention symbolic, unless
asked to complete the model:

```{r}
w <- z3_int(ctx, "w")
z3_eval(m, x + w)
z3_eval(m, x + w, completion = TRUE)
```

A model belongs to one check. When the solver changes, z3r refuses to hand
out a model until the next check, so a model never describes constraints it
was not computed for:

```{r, error = TRUE}
z3_add(s, x > 100)
z3_model(s)
```

The model already retrieved stays valid as a snapshot.

Models can also be built by hand, to evaluate formulas under chosen values:

```{r}
m2 <- z3_model(ctx)
z3_model_set(m2, x, 4)
z3_model_set(m2, y, 7)
z3_eval(m2, x * y + 1)
```

## Incremental solving

Push and pop scopes to explore variations without rebuilding the problem:

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x >= 0, x <= 10)
z3_push(s)
z3_add(s, x > 20)
z3_check(s)
z3_pop(s)
z3_check(s)
z3_num_scopes(s)
```

Assumptions hold for one check only:

```{r}
z3_check(s, x == 3)
z3_check(s, x == 30)
z3_assertions(s)
```

`z3_with_scope()` pops for you, even when the code inside fails:

```{r}
z3_with_scope(s, {
  z3_add(s, x > 20)
  z3_check(s)
})
z3_num_scopes(s)
```

## Enumerating solutions

`z3_all_models()` lists distinct assignments of some variables by blocking
each one found. The `"status"` attribute says whether all were found
(`"unsat"`), the limit was reached, or Z3 gave up:

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x >= 0, y >= 0, x + 2 * y == 6)
sols <- z3_all_models(s, list(x, y))
do.call(rbind, lapply(sols, as.data.frame))
attr(sols, "status")
```

## Unsatisfiable cores

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_assert_and_track(s, x > 10, "x_big")
z3_assert_and_track(s, x < 5, "x_small")
z3_assert_and_track(s, y == 2, "y_two")
z3_check(s)
names(z3_unsat_core(s))
```

The core names a subset of the labelled constraints that is already
contradictory; `y_two` is not in it. Cores are not guaranteed minimal. The
same works with assumptions:

```{r}
a <- z3_bools(ctx, c("a1", "a2", "a3"))
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, z3_implies(a$a1, x > 5), z3_implies(a$a2, x < 3), z3_implies(a$a3, y == 1))
z3_check(s, a$a1, a$a2, a$a3)
names(z3_unsat_core(s))
```

## Proofs

A context created with `proof = TRUE` records proofs of unsatisfiability:

```{r}
pctx <- z3_context(proof = TRUE)
p <- z3_bool(pctx, "p")
q <- z3_bool(pctx, "q")
s <- z3_solver(pctx)
z3_add(s, z3_implies(p, q), p, !q)
z3_check(s)
substr(format(z3_proof(s)), 1, 200)
```

## Consequences, cubes and the trail

`z3_consequences()` reports which literals over chosen variables follow
from the assertions and assumptions:

```{r}
p <- z3_bools(ctx, c("p", "q", "r"))
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, z3_implies(p$p, p$q), z3_implies(p$q, p$r))
z3_consequences(s, list(p$p), list(p$q, p$r))$consequences
```

`z3_cube()` splits the search space for cube-and-conquer parallelism, and a
simple solver (`z3_solver(ctx, simple = TRUE)`) exposes its decision trail:

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx, simple = TRUE)
z3_add(s, p$p, z3_or(p$q, p$r))
z3_check(s)
z3_trail(s)
```

## Validity: proving instead of finding

A formula is valid (true for every value) exactly when its negation is
unsatisfiable:

```{r}
prove <- function(ctx, formula) {
  s <- z3_solver(ctx)
  z3_add(s, !formula)
  switch(z3_check(s), unsat = "valid", sat = "not valid", unknown = "unknown")
}
prove(ctx, (x + y)^2 == x^2 + 2 * x * y + y^2)
prove(ctx, (x + y)^2 == x^2 + y^2)
```

## Logic-specific and tactic-based solvers

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx, logic = "QF_LIA")
z3_add(s, 3 * x + 2 * y == 17, x >= 0, y >= 0)
z3_check(s)
head(unlist(z3_statistics(s)), 6)
```

`z3_statistics_text()` gives the same statistics as Z3 prints them.

## Time limits and interruption

`timeout` limits one check to that many milliseconds; a check that runs out
of time returns `"unknown"`, and the solver keeps its own settings for the
next check:

```{r}
s <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(s, x * x * x + y * y * y == 33, x > 0)
r <- z3_check(s, timeout = 50)
r
if (r == "unknown") z3_reason_unknown(s)
```

Inside a callback (`vignette("propagators")`), `z3_interrupt(s)` stops the
running check, which then returns `"unknown"` with the reason
`"interrupted"`.

`vignette("tactics")` shows solvers built from tactics, and
`vignette("propagators")` shows how R code can join the search.
